newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr National falls on outlook worries.
newsitem.headline: Cr National falls on outlook worries.

text.p: French bank Credit National was down sharply on continued disappointment at its half-year results and market rumours that its credit rating might be downgraded.
At 1455 GMT, the share was off 7.81 percent at 236.0 francs in volume of 167,222 shares. There was no comment from Credit National on the rumours.
"The company is continuing its descent brought on by its results," said one trader. "It had a half year loss, its outlook isn't good."

The company's shares have lost more than 20 percent of their value since the company announced on September 25 that it plunged to a 112 million franc ($21.7 million) loss from a profit of 267 million francs a year earlier.
The loss was due to provisions of 250 million francs for restructuring in wake of buying Banque Francaise de Commerce Exterieur (BFCE).
Credit rating agency IBCA said on September 30 it might downgrade its short-term and long-term debt due to the poor half year results.
The bank has said that its aim was to get back above breakeven for the year as a whole.
